question:
Three pure crystalline solids $P,Q,R$ have the following simplified band descriptions at $0\,\text{K}$:

- Solid $P$: Conduction band overlaps the valence band by $0.10\,\text{eV}$.
- Solid $Q$: Band gap $E_g=0.70\,\text{eV}$.
- Solid $R$: Band gap $E_g=3.50\,\text{eV}$.

(a) Classify each solid as conductor / semiconductor / insulator using band theory at $0\,\text{K}$.

(b) At $300\,\text{K}$, arrange their conductivities in descending order with clear justification from band theory.

(c) When temperature is increased from $300\,\text{K}$ to $500\,\text{K}$, identify which solid shows the largest fractional increase in conductivity and justify using temperature dependence of carrier concentration.

(d) Suggest the most suitable solid among $P,Q,R$ for each application and justify: 

(i) heating element wire, 

(ii) thermistor-type temperature sensor, 

(iii) dielectric/insulating layer in a capacitor. 

(e) Draw qualitative energy band diagrams for $P,Q,R$ showing overlap/gap clearly and label the key features.

options.A: $P$ conductor, $Q$ semiconductor, $R$ insulator; at $300\,\text{K}$: $\sigma_P>\sigma_Q\gg\sigma_R$; largest fractional increase: $Q$; applications: $(i)P,(ii)Q,(iii)R$.
options.B: $P$ insulator, $Q$ conductor, $R$ semiconductor; at $300\,\text{K}$: $\sigma_Q>\sigma_R>\sigma_P$; largest fractional increase: $P$; applications: $(i)Q,(ii)R,(iii)P$.
options.C: $P$ semiconductor, $Q$ insulator, $R$ conductor; at $300\,\text{K}$: $\sigma_R>\sigma_P>\sigma_Q$; largest fractional increase: $R$; applications: $(i)R,(ii)P,(iii)Q$.
options.D: $P$ conductor, $Q$ insulator, $R$ semiconductor; at $300\,\text{K}$: $\sigma_P>\sigma_R>\sigma_Q$; largest fractional increase: $R$; applications: $(i)P,(ii)R,(iii)Q$.
